ma [491], pron. root, see ahám. [cf. μέ,
Lat. me, AS. mē, Eng. me.]

√1mā (mímīte [660-3]; mamaú, mamé;
ámāsta; mitá [954c]; mā́tum; mitvā́;
-mā́ya).
 —1. measure;
 —2. measure
with, compare;
 —3. mete out;
 —4. arrange,
 form; build; make, 72^2. [for 1,
cf. μέ-τρον, ‘measure’; Lat. ni-mi-us, ‘not
to be measured, excessive’; for 4, cf.
μά-ρη and Lat. mă-nu-s, ‘former, i. e. hand’;
εὐ-μαρής, ‘handy, easy’: see also the collateral
form √1mi, ‘build, set up,’ and
under mātṛ́ and mā́s.]
+ anu, (form after, i. e.) re-create in
imagination, conceive.
+ upa, measure with, compare.
+ nis, fashion or make out of (abl.); construct.
+ vi-nis, lay out (garden).
+ pari, measure around, limit.
+ pra, measure.
+ prati, make (so as to be a match)
against, cf. pratimā.
+ vi, measure out; then (like Eng. measure),
 pass over, traverse (the sky).

√2mā or mī (mímāti [660-3]; mimā́ya).
bellow.
+ vi, bellow or cry aloud.
